concepts.name: Asymptotic complexity analysis
concepts.description: State the time and space complexity of code you wrote or read, and justify the bound rather than pattern-matching it.

concepts.name: Amortized analysis
concepts.description: Reason about cost averaged over a sequence of operations, e.g. why dynamic-array append is O(1) amortized despite occasional resizes.

concepts.name: Space complexity and in-place work
concepts.description: Account for auxiliary memory separately from input, and recognize when a solution can be made in-place.

concepts.name: Edge-case enumeration
concepts.description: Systematically surface empty inputs, single elements, duplicates, overflow, and boundary indices before claiming a solution is correct.

concepts.name: Clarifying an underspecified problem
concepts.description: Ask the questions that change the solution — input bounds, duplicates, mutability, return shape — before writing code.

concepts.name: Communicating a solution and its cost
concepts.description: Narrate an approach and its tradeoffs out loud so an interviewer can follow the reasoning without reading the code.

concepts.name: Readable interview code
concepts.description: Write code a reviewer can follow under time pressure: meaningful names, small functions, no dead branches.

concepts.name: Two pointers
concepts.description: Collapse a nested scan into a linear one by advancing two indices under an ordering or monotonicity invariant.

concepts.name: Sliding window
concepts.description: Maintain a contiguous window and its aggregate under an admissibility condition, expanding and contracting in amortized linear time.

concepts.name: Prefix sums and difference arrays
concepts.description: Precompute cumulative aggregates so range queries or range updates become constant time.

concepts.name: In-place array mutation
concepts.description: Rearrange, partition, or compact an array using O(1) extra space while preserving the required invariant.

concepts.name: String parsing and tokenization
concepts.description: Walk a string with explicit state, handling delimiters, escapes, and malformed input without regex crutches.

concepts.name: Hash map counting and lookup
concepts.description: Trade memory for time by indexing values, frequencies, or last-seen positions in a hash map.

concepts.name: Hash set membership
concepts.description: Use set membership for dedup and cycle/seen detection, and know when a set is the wrong structure.

concepts.name: Composite and custom hash keys
concepts.description: Design a key that captures the equivalence you actually want — sorted signatures, tuples, canonical forms — and reason about collisions.

concepts.name: Sorting and custom comparators
concepts.description: Choose a sort key or comparator that makes the rest of the problem easy, and know the n log n lower bound and when it can be beaten.

concepts.name: Binary search over an index
concepts.description: Search a sorted or rotated array with a loop invariant that provably terminates and does not skip the boundary.
tags: find minimum in rotated sorted array

concepts.name: Binary search on the answer
concepts.description: Turn an optimization into a monotone feasibility predicate and binary search the answer space.
tags: capacity to ship packages within d days
minimum days to make m bouquets

concepts.name: Linked list manipulation
concepts.description: Rewire pointers correctly — reversal, splicing, merging — without losing nodes or creating cycles.
tags: remove nth node from end of list

concepts.name: Fast and slow pointers
concepts.description: Detect cycles and find midpoints or cycle entries using pointers advancing at different rates.

concepts.name: Stack-based simulation
concepts.description: Use a stack to track nested or deferred state — bracket matching, expression evaluation, undo semantics.

concepts.name: Monotonic stack
concepts.description: Maintain a stack under a monotonicity invariant to answer next-greater and span queries in linear time.

concepts.name: Monotonic deque over a window
concepts.description: Keep a double-ended queue ordered so window extrema are available in O(1) as the window slides.
tags: shortest subarray with sum at least k

concepts.name: Tree traversal
concepts.description: Traverse trees in pre/in/post/level order, iteratively as well as recursively, and pick the order the problem requires.

concepts.name: Binary search tree invariants
concepts.description: Exploit and preserve BST ordering for search, insert, delete, and validation.
tags: kth smallest element in a bst
lowest common ancestor of a binary search tree
insert into a binary search tree

concepts.name: Dynamic programming on trees
concepts.description: Compute per-subtree answers bottom-up and combine them at each node.
tags: count good nodes in binary tree

concepts.name: Lowest common ancestor
concepts.description: Find LCA by recursive descent or ancestor sets, and reason about the tradeoffs with preprocessing.
tags: lowest common ancestor of a binary tree

concepts.name: Tries and prefix structures
concepts.description: Store strings by shared prefix to make prefix queries and autocomplete linear in the query length.

concepts.name: Heaps and top-k selection
concepts.description: Use a bounded heap to keep the k best elements in a stream without sorting everything.
tags: kth largest element in an array

concepts.name: Two-heap running median
concepts.description: Balance a max-heap and a min-heap to expose the median of a stream in constant time.

concepts.name: Recursion and base cases
concepts.description: Decompose a problem into a smaller instance of itself with a base case that provably terminates.

concepts.name: Backtracking search
concepts.description: Enumerate a constrained solution space with pruning, undoing state correctly on the way back up.
tags: letter combinations of a phone number

concepts.name: Memoization
concepts.description: Cache subproblem results keyed on the state that actually determines the answer.

concepts.name: One-dimensional dynamic programming
concepts.description: Define a linear state, a recurrence, and a base case, then fill iteratively — and identify the state, which is the hard part.

concepts.name: Grid and two-sequence DP
concepts.description: Fill a two-dimensional table for path counting, edit distance, and sequence alignment problems.

concepts.name: DP on subsequences
concepts.description: Handle longest-increasing and subset-selection recurrences where the state is a chosen prefix plus a constraint.

concepts.name: Knapsack-family DP
concepts.description: Model bounded and unbounded selection under a capacity constraint, and compress the table when only the previous row matters.

concepts.name: Interval DP
concepts.description: Solve over ranges by splitting at an interior point — matrix chain, burst balloons, palindromic partitions.
tags: minimum cost to cut a stick

concepts.name: Greedy with an exchange argument
concepts.description: Justify a greedy choice by showing any optimal solution can be transformed into one that makes it, rather than asserting it works.
tags: minimum number of arrows to burst balloons

concepts.name: Interval scheduling by end time
concepts.description: Sort by the right endpoint and take each interval that starts after the last one kept, to schedule the most non-conflicting intervals or remove the fewest overlapping ones — and say why choosing the earliest finish cannot lose.
tags: minimum number of arrows to burst balloons

concepts.name: Breadth-first search
concepts.description: Explore level by level for shortest paths in unweighted graphs, tracking visited state correctly.

concepts.name: Depth-first search
concepts.description: Explore deeply for connectivity, cycle detection, and component labeling, iteratively when recursion would overflow.
tags: all paths from source to target

concepts.name: Grids as graphs
concepts.description: Treat a matrix as an implicit graph with neighbor generation and boundary handling.

concepts.name: Topological ordering
concepts.description: Order a DAG by dependency and detect the cycle that makes ordering impossible.

concepts.name: Disjoint set union
concepts.description: Maintain dynamic connectivity with path compression and union by rank, and know the near-constant amortized cost.

concepts.name: Weighted shortest paths
concepts.description: Apply Dijkstra with a priority queue, and recognize when negative weights rule it out.

concepts.name: Bitmask state and subset enumeration
concepts.description: Encode a small set as an integer to enumerate subsets or index DP states compactly.
tags: partition to k equal sum subsets

concepts.name: Bit manipulation
concepts.description: Use XOR, masks, and shifts deliberately — parity, single-number, low-bit isolation — and reason about signedness.

concepts.name: Class and interface design
concepts.description: Choose responsibilities and boundaries for a small object model under an interview-scale requirement.

concepts.name: Data-structure design under constraints
concepts.description: Compose primitives to hit stated per-operation complexity targets, as in LRU cache or O(1) insert-delete-random.

concepts.name: Iterator and lazy evaluation design
concepts.description: Expose a streaming interface that computes on demand rather than materializing everything.

concepts.name: Thread safety fundamentals
concepts.description: Identify shared mutable state, races, and deadlock, and reason about what a lock actually protects.

concepts.name: Single-pass running best (Kadane)
concepts.description: Carry a running minimum, maximum or best-so-far through one scan so the answer is updated in O(1) per element — maximum subarray, best time to buy and sell stock, maximum product subarray — and say why one pass is enough.
tags: best time to buy and sell stock

concepts.name: Constant-space array tricks
concepts.description: Use the array itself as the extra memory: cyclic sort and sign-marking for values in 1..n, Floyd's cycle trick on indices, and Boyer–Moore majority vote — and explain why each is O(1) space and still linear time.
tags: find all duplicates in an array

concepts.name: Matrix rotation, spiral and layered traversal
concepts.description: Walk or transform a 2D grid by layers, diagonals or transposition — rotate in place, spiral order, set matrix zeroes — keeping the boundary indices right on non-square input.

concepts.name: Counting sort and bucketing
concepts.description: Sort or select in linear time when keys are bounded: counting sort, bucketing by frequency, and the Dutch-flag partition — and recognise when the bound makes n log n unnecessary.

concepts.name: Integer arithmetic and number theory
concepts.description: Manipulate digits, avoid overflow, and use gcd, modular arithmetic, fast exponentiation and closed-form sums — plus digit-by-digit arithmetic on numbers held as strings.

concepts.name: Points, lines and rectangles
concepts.description: Compare slopes as reduced fractions, distances without square roots, and rectangle overlap or containment — and hash a point or a direction so equal ones collide.

concepts.name: Randomised selection and sampling
concepts.description: Sample uniformly from a stream or a structure of unknown size (reservoir sampling), shuffle in place (Fisher–Yates), and pick by weight with prefix sums and binary search — and argue the distribution is right.

concepts.name: Palindrome structure
concepts.description: Check and find palindromes: two pointers from the ends, expanding around each centre for the longest palindromic substring or its count, and knowing when a DP table or Manacher is needed instead.

concepts.name: Substring search and rolling hash
concepts.description: Find a pattern in text faster than the naive scan — Rabin–Karp with a rolling hash, the KMP failure function, or a Z-array — and reason about collisions and worst cases.
tags: find the index of the first occurrence in a string

concepts.name: Merging and inserting intervals
concepts.description: Sort intervals by start and sweep once to merge overlaps, insert a new interval into a sorted list, or intersect two lists — and decide whether touching endpoints count as overlapping.

concepts.name: Sweep line and overlap counting
concepts.description: Count how many intervals are live at once by sweeping sorted endpoints or keeping a min-heap of end times — meeting rooms II, minimum platforms, car pooling, the skyline — and answer how many are open at a given time.
tags: minimum interval to include each query

concepts.name: Building and serialising trees
concepts.description: Reconstruct a tree from traversal orders, serialise and deserialise it, and build a balanced tree from a sorted sequence, choosing the traversal whose order makes the recursion simple.
tags: construct binary tree from preorder and inorder traversal
construct binary tree from inorder and postorder

concepts.name: Segment trees and Fenwick trees
concepts.description: Answer range queries under point updates in logarithmic time with a Fenwick tree or a segment tree, and know when a plain prefix sum or a sorted container already suffices.
tags: count of smaller numbers after self

concepts.name: K-way merge with a heap
concepts.description: Merge k sorted sequences by keeping one frontier element per sequence in a heap — merge k sorted lists, kth smallest in a sorted matrix, smallest range covering every list — in O(n log k).
tags: kth smallest element in a sorted matrix
smallest range covering elements from k lists
find k pairs with smallest sums

concepts.name: Priority-queue driven scheduling
concepts.description: Drive a simulation from a heap — pop the most urgent or most frequent element, apply it, push it back changed — for task scheduling, reorganising a string, meeting rooms by end time, and a streaming kth-largest.
tags: kth largest element in a stream

concepts.name: Sorted containers and ordered maps
concepts.description: Keep a sorted collection under insertions and answer predecessor, successor and range questions in log time — via bisect on a list, a sorted container, or a balanced tree — as in a booking calendar or a time-based key-value store.

concepts.name: Bipartite check and two-colouring
concepts.description: Two-colour a graph by BFS or DFS to test bipartiteness, and translate 'split into two groups with no conflict inside a group' into that test.

concepts.name: BFS over an implicit state space
concepts.description: Search a graph whose nodes are states rather than a given adjacency list — word ladder, open the lock, a grid with keys or obstacle removals — hashing the state, seeding several sources at once, and pruning with a visited set.
tags: shortest path to get all keys

concepts.name: Minimum spanning tree
concepts.description: Connect every node at minimum total cost with Kruskal over sorted edges and a disjoint set, or Prim with a heap, and say which fits a dense versus a sparse graph.
tags: min cost to connect all points
optimize water distribution in a village

concepts.name: Eulerian paths and Hierholzer's algorithm
concepts.description: Use every edge exactly once — reconstruct an itinerary, find a valid arrangement of pairs — by checking the degree conditions and building the path with Hierholzer's post-order trick.

concepts.name: Bellman–Ford and bounded-edge shortest paths
concepts.description: Relax every edge in rounds to handle negative weights, a cap on the number of edges, or negative-cycle detection — cheapest flights within k stops — and know when Dijkstra is wrong for it.

concepts.name: Bridges, articulation points and SCCs
concepts.description: Find the edges or vertices whose removal disconnects a graph with Tarjan's low-link DFS, and extend the same discovery-time bookkeeping to strongly connected components.

concepts.name: State-machine DP
concepts.description: Add a small discrete state to a linear DP — holding or not holding a stock, a cooldown, transactions left, the previous choice — and write one transition per state rather than one giant recurrence.
tags: best time to buy and sell stock with cooldown
best time to buy and sell stock iii
best time to buy and sell stock iv

concepts.name: Minimax and game DP
concepts.description: Decide who wins a two-player perfect-information game by recursing on the state with the players' objectives alternating, memoising positions, and recognising the closed-form parity cases.
tags: guess number higher or lower ii

concepts.name: Divide and conquer
concepts.description: Split, solve the halves and combine — merge sort and counting inversions, quickselect for the kth element, the closest pair — and derive the recurrence's cost.
tags: kth largest element in an array

concepts.name: Frontier and reachability greedy
concepts.description: Sweep once carrying the furthest reach, the running surplus or the last boundary — jump game, gas station, partition labels — and argue why the local update cannot lose the optimum.

concepts.name: Faithful simulation
concepts.description: Implement a stated process exactly as specified — a robot's moves, a game-of-life step, a spiral walk, a parking lot — keeping state explicit and boundaries right, without hunting for a shortcut that is not there.

concepts.name: Sample spaces and counting
concepts.description: Set up the right sample space and count outcomes without double-counting or conflating ordered and unordered.

concepts.name: Permutations and combinations
concepts.description: Count arrangements and selections, with and without replacement, and recognize which the problem asks for.

concepts.name: Inclusion-exclusion
concepts.description: Count unions of overlapping events by alternating over intersections.

concepts.name: Symmetry arguments
concepts.description: Collapse a messy computation by arguing that outcomes are exchangeable — a signature quant-interview move.

concepts.name: Pigeonhole and extremal arguments
concepts.description: Prove existence by counting, without constructing the object.

concepts.name: Conditional probability
concepts.description: Condition correctly on information, and avoid the base-rate and selection traps that follow.

concepts.name: Bayes' rule
concepts.description: Invert a conditional to update a prior with evidence, and state the answer in odds form when it is cleaner.

concepts.name: Independence and its failure
concepts.description: Test independence rather than assuming it, and notice when conditioning destroys or creates it.

concepts.name: Bernoulli and binomial
concepts.description: Model repeated independent trials and compute their mean, variance, and tail behavior.

concepts.name: Geometric and negative binomial
concepts.description: Model waiting times in discrete trials, and use memorylessness to shortcut the algebra.

concepts.name: Poisson processes
concepts.description: Model rare events in continuous time, including superposition, thinning, and interarrival times.

concepts.name: Exponential and memorylessness
concepts.description: Use the memoryless property to solve competing-risk and minimum-of-exponentials problems.

concepts.name: Uniforms and order statistics
concepts.description: Reason about the distribution of the k-th smallest of n draws, and the spacings between them.

concepts.name: Normal distribution and the CLT
concepts.description: Apply the central limit theorem to approximate sums, and use normal tail heuristics for quick estimates.

concepts.name: Linearity of expectation
concepts.description: Sum expectations of dependent quantities without touching the joint distribution — the highest-leverage tool in the toolbox.

concepts.name: Indicator random variables
concepts.description: Decompose a count into indicators so linearity applies, even when the events are heavily dependent.

concepts.name: Law of total expectation
concepts.description: Condition on the first step to set up a recursion for an expected value.

concepts.name: Variance and covariance
concepts.description: Compute variance of sums with covariance terms, and interpret correlation as a normalized covariance.

concepts.name: Conditional expectation as a random variable
concepts.description: Treat E[X|Y] as a function of Y and use the tower property fluently.

concepts.name: Random walks
concepts.description: Analyze symmetric and biased walks: hitting probabilities, expected durations, and recurrence.

concepts.name: Gambler's ruin
concepts.description: Solve absorption probabilities and expected times for a bounded walk, in the fair and biased cases.

concepts.name: Markov chains and absorption
concepts.description: Set up state equations for hitting times and absorption probabilities, and solve the resulting linear system.

concepts.name: Martingales and optional stopping
concepts.description: Construct a martingale and apply optional stopping to read off an answer that would otherwise need heavy algebra.

concepts.name: Brownian motion fundamentals
concepts.description: Use independent stationary Gaussian increments, scaling, and the reflection principle at an interview level.

concepts.name: Decision-making under expectation
concepts.description: Choose between actions by expected value, and say explicitly when expected value is the wrong objective.

concepts.name: Bet sizing and the Kelly criterion
concepts.description: Size a bet to maximize long-run growth rather than expected value, and explain why the two differ.

concepts.name: Two-player game reasoning
concepts.description: Find optimal play by backward induction or a mixed-strategy equilibrium in small games.

concepts.name: Auctions and the winner's curse
concepts.description: Reason about bidding when winning is itself information about your valuation.

concepts.name: Adverse selection
concepts.description: Recognize that a counterparty's willingness to trade carries information, and price it in.

concepts.name: Fair value and edge
concepts.description: Compute a fair value from available information and express a quote as fair value plus a spread for uncertainty.

concepts.name: Quoting a two-sided market
concepts.description: Set a bid and an ask that stay profitable against an informed counterparty, and widen when uncertainty rises.

concepts.name: Inventory and position risk
concepts.description: Skew quotes to manage accumulated position, trading expected edge against variance.

concepts.name: P&L attribution
concepts.description: Decompose a result into edge, market move, and noise instead of reading outcome as skill.

concepts.name: Fast fraction and percentage arithmetic
concepts.description: Convert and combine fractions, decimals, and percentages accurately at speed, without a calculator.

concepts.name: Mental multiplication and division
concepts.description: Multiply and divide multi-digit numbers using decomposition and difference-of-squares tricks under time pressure.

concepts.name: Logs, exponents, and roots by estimation
concepts.description: Approximate powers, roots, and logarithms well enough to sanity-check an answer in seconds.

concepts.name: Compounding and growth estimation
concepts.description: Apply the rule of 72 and first-order approximations to growth and discounting questions.

concepts.name: Fermi estimation
concepts.description: Decompose an unknown quantity into estimable factors and defend each assumption.

concepts.name: Order-of-magnitude sanity checking
concepts.description: Catch an answer that is wrong by a factor of a thousand before stating it.

concepts.name: Sampling and selection bias
concepts.description: Identify how data was selected and what that does to any inference drawn from it.

concepts.name: Hypothesis testing intuition
concepts.description: Reason about signal versus noise, sample size, and what a p-value does and does not claim.

concepts.name: Correlation traps
concepts.description: Handle spurious correlation, non-stationarity, and the fact that correlation is not transitive.

concepts.name: Linear regression intuition
concepts.description: Interpret coefficients, R-squared, and residuals, and explain regression to the mean.

concepts.name: No-arbitrage reasoning
concepts.description: Price by replication: if two portfolios pay the same, they cost the same, or there is free money.

concepts.name: Time value and discounting
concepts.description: Move cash flows through time correctly and reason about interest-rate conventions.

concepts.name: Put-call parity
concepts.description: Relate calls, puts, forwards, and cash by replication, and use it to sanity-check a quoted price.

concepts.name: Option sensitivities
concepts.description: Reason qualitatively about delta, gamma, vega, and theta without deriving Black-Scholes.

concepts.name: Sequence and pattern puzzles
concepts.description: Infer a generating rule from a short sequence and justify it rather than guessing.

concepts.name: Invariant and monovariant arguments
concepts.description: Find a quantity preserved by every legal move to prove a configuration unreachable.

concepts.name: Parity arguments
concepts.description: Use odd/even invariants to settle reachability and tiling questions instantly.

concepts.name: Information-theoretic puzzles
concepts.description: Bound the number of measurements needed by counting distinguishable outcomes — weighings, guessing games, sorting bounds.

concepts.name: Functional requirements
concepts.description: Extract the concrete features in scope and state explicitly what is out of scope.

concepts.name: Non-functional requirements
concepts.description: Pin down latency, availability, consistency, and durability targets before designing anything.

concepts.name: Scoping and tradeoff framing
concepts.description: Choose what to design deeply and name the tradeoff you are making rather than presenting one option.

concepts.name: Capacity estimation
concepts.description: Estimate QPS, storage, and bandwidth from user numbers, and let the result drive the design.

concepts.name: Latency budgets
concepts.description: Decompose an end-to-end target into per-hop budgets and identify which hop dominates.

concepts.name: API contract design
concepts.description: Define endpoints, payloads, and error semantics that make the client's job easy and the server's job possible.

concepts.name: Idempotency
concepts.description: Make retries safe with idempotency keys and well-defined at-least-once semantics.

concepts.name: Pagination and streaming results
concepts.description: Choose cursor over offset pagination when the underlying data changes, and explain why.

concepts.name: Data modeling
concepts.description: Design entities, relationships, and access patterns, letting the queries drive the schema.

concepts.name: Storage engine selection
concepts.description: Justify a relational, document, key-value, or column store from the access pattern rather than by reflex.

concepts.name: Indexing
concepts.description: Choose indexes from the read path and account for their write and storage cost.

concepts.name: Sharding and partitioning
concepts.description: Pick a partition key that spreads load without creating hot spots, and handle resharding.

concepts.name: Replication
concepts.description: Reason about leader-follower and multi-leader replication, replication lag, and read-your-writes.

concepts.name: Caching strategies
concepts.description: Place caches deliberately — client, CDN, application, database — and know what each buys.

concepts.name: Cache invalidation and staleness
concepts.description: Choose TTL, write-through, or explicit invalidation, and state the staleness the design accepts.

concepts.name: CDN and edge delivery
concepts.description: Push static and cacheable content to the edge and reason about cache keys and purges.

concepts.name: Queues and backpressure
concepts.description: Decouple producers from consumers, and decide what happens when the queue grows without bound.

concepts.name: Pub/sub and fanout
concepts.description: Distribute one event to many consumers, choosing between fanout-on-write and fanout-on-read.

concepts.name: Event-driven architecture
concepts.description: Model state changes as events, with ordering and replay semantics stated explicitly.

concepts.name: Delivery semantics
concepts.description: Distinguish at-most-once, at-least-once, and effectively-once, and explain why true exactly-once is a claim to interrogate.

concepts.name: Load balancing
concepts.description: Distribute traffic across instances and reason about health checks, algorithms, and sticky sessions.

concepts.name: Stateless services
concepts.description: Push state out of the service tier so instances scale and fail independently.

concepts.name: Horizontal scaling
concepts.description: Scale out rather than up, and identify the component that becomes the bottleneck when you do.

concepts.name: Rate limiting and quotas
concepts.description: Protect a service with token bucket or sliding window limits, applied at the right granularity.

concepts.name: Consistency models
concepts.description: Distinguish strong, causal, and eventual consistency and pick the weakest one the product tolerates.

concepts.name: CAP and partition behavior
concepts.description: State what the system does during a partition, which is the only form of the CAP question worth asking.

concepts.name: Failure-mode analysis
concepts.description: Walk each component and say what happens when it fails, degrades, or comes back.

concepts.name: Retries, timeouts, and jitter
concepts.description: Set timeouts and bounded retries with backoff and jitter, avoiding retry storms.

concepts.name: Circuit breaking and graceful degradation
concepts.description: Shed load and fail fast so one slow dependency does not take down the system.

concepts.name: Observability
concepts.description: Instrument with metrics, structured logs, and traces, and say which question each one answers.

concepts.name: SLIs, SLOs, and error budgets
concepts.description: Define measurable objectives and use the error budget to arbitrate reliability against velocity.

concepts.name: Authentication and authorization
concepts.description: Separate identity from permission and place enforcement where it cannot be bypassed.

concepts.name: Secrets management
concepts.description: Keep credentials out of code and images, with rotation and least privilege as defaults.

concepts.name: Physical latency limits
concepts.description: Reason from speed-of-light, colocation, and switch-hop costs — the floor no software can beat.

concepts.name: Hot-path design
concepts.description: Remove allocation, locking, and branching from the critical path, and measure rather than assume.

concepts.name: Kernel bypass and userspace networking
concepts.description: Explain what bypassing the kernel network stack buys and what it costs in complexity.

concepts.name: Determinism and replay
concepts.description: Design a system whose output can be reproduced byte-for-byte from a recorded input sequence.

concepts.name: STAR structure
concepts.description: Deliver a story with a clear situation, task, action, and result, without drifting into background.

concepts.name: Concise situation framing
concepts.description: Give exactly the context needed to make the rest of the story land, in under thirty seconds.

concepts.name: Quantified impact
concepts.description: Close a story with a measured outcome rather than an assertion that it went well.

concepts.name: Narrative concision
concepts.description: Keep an answer to two minutes without losing the point, and stop when the question is answered.

concepts.name: Ownership and initiative
concepts.description: Show that you identified a problem nobody assigned you and carried it to a result.

concepts.name: Disagreement and conflict
concepts.description: Describe a real technical or interpersonal disagreement and how it resolved, without villainizing anyone.

concepts.name: Failure and what changed after
concepts.description: Tell a story about a genuine failure you caused, and name the specific behavior that changed.

concepts.name: Operating under ambiguity
concepts.description: Show how you made progress when the goal, the data, or the priority was undefined.

concepts.name: Influence without authority
concepts.description: Describe changing a decision you had no power to make, and what actually persuaded people.

concepts.name: Prioritization under constraint
concepts.description: Explain what you chose not to do, and the reasoning that made that the right call.

concepts.name: Collaboration and mentoring
concepts.description: Show you made the people around you more effective, with a concrete instance.

concepts.name: Resume project deep dive
concepts.description: Explain a project on your resume at increasing depth without hitting a floor you cannot defend.

concepts.name: Defending a technical decision
concepts.description: Justify a design choice you made, including the alternative you rejected and why.

concepts.name: Honest attribution
concepts.description: State precisely which parts were yours on a team project — vagueness here reads as inflation.

concepts.name: Handling pushback
concepts.description: Hold or update a position under interviewer pressure based on the argument, not the pressure.

concepts.name: Listening and clarifying
concepts.description: Answer the question that was actually asked, checking first when it is ambiguous.

concepts.name: Firm-specific motivation
concepts.description: Give a reason for this firm that could not be copy-pasted to a competitor.

concepts.name: Motivation for quant trading
concepts.description: Explain the pull toward trading in terms of the work itself, not compensation or prestige.

concepts.name: Coherent career narrative
concepts.description: Connect what you have done to what you are asking to do next, so the move reads as deliberate.
